title_zh: 便宜、庞大、会创新，然后呢
deck_zh: 把几位老读者请到同一张桌前，不为找人站队，而为听清那些不能轻轻放过的问题。
deck_en: Price, bigness, and innovation ask different things of an economy. The difficult conversation begins when more than one answer is true.
body_zh: 通衢又降价了。店主算了算，这个月能省下一笔，顾客也多买了些东西。如果有人这时说，先别高兴，我们还得谈垄断，他很可能会皱眉：你们谈的自由，能不能先让我少交一点钱？这个反问值得认真听。否则，一套本来关心人的想法，也可能只关心自己的词。
读到这里，离得开、有的选、问得动，已经成了熟悉的几句话。可一句话熟悉以后，也会有新的危险：拿到哪里都觉得自己答对了。最后这一篇，不再添一个万能答案，而是请几种有分量的问法进来，让我们看看手里的工具，哪里够用，哪里还得往前做。
先从价格说起。斯密在《国富论》第一篇第七章，对照垄断价格与自由竞争的价格：前者尽量从买者那里取得高价，后者则受到维持经营所需条件的约束。这是一条清楚的观察路径。控制者若能让东西长期供不应求，顾客便可能为那个位置多付钱。
价格重要，不只是因为它容易画成图。多花的钱，会挤掉一家人的别的安排；少花的钱，也真能松开一点生活。不能为了突出自己的新问题，就把已经得到的便宜说成幻觉。店主省下的费用、顾客买得起的日用品，都应该留在账里。
可是通衢还可以更便宜，同时不让店主带走有用的交易记录。新平台愿意接他，旧记录却只能导出一堆读不进新系统的文件。价格那一栏变好了，离开的那一栏没有。我们需要把第二件事加进去，不必先宣布第一件事不算数。
这也不是对斯密整部著作下一个只看价格的断语。我们在这里借他的一条具体分析，辨清它照到了什么，再问另一个问题。若一位重视价格的读者反问，迁移的难处究竟多大、值多少钱、是不是你们想象出来的，那是我们今天必须回答的追问，不是假托古人已经说过的话。
回答应当走到店里：他需要哪些记录，新系统到底读不了什么，补录要多久，是否有安全与他人隐私的理由。不能把不方便三个字直接扩成被控制，也不能拿每月便宜二十元，替所有迁移条件作结论。两笔账得放到同一张桌上，但不能相互涂掉。
再请进来的，是布兰代斯。《别人的钱》第八章题为大之诅咒，标题很容易让人以为，他只要见到大公司就反对。正文中有一条更值得留下的线索：规模如何取得，又被拿来做什么。形成的手段与使用的方向，是可以分别看的。
这使今天的好用，不能自动洗掉昨天的封路。设若一家企业曾经用不正当的办法排挤对手，后来确实改进了服务，我们可以承认改进，也可以追究已经发生的事。反过来，它当年的贡献，也不能给今天的排他安排发一张永久通行证。
看现在，不等于从今天起失忆。过去行为的责任、过去留下而仍在起作用的安排、今天采取什么措施，至少是三件事。它们有关联，却不是同一句话。旧责任怎样影响今天措施的根据与分量，还需要具体工作；这一组文章没有替它们算出一条通用换算式。
布兰代斯的讨论也带来一个时间上的催问：是不是总要等合并完成、依赖长成，再请受影响的人来证明自己受了多少损失？在他援引的铁路监管建议中，事前批准与限制已经站在很重要的位置。预先留下约束，不只是出事以后的补救。
不过，把时间提早，并不自动使判断正确。早期限制也可能挡住一次有用的合作。提出合并的一方得说明会带来什么，主张约束的一方也得说明担心什么、根据何在、代价怎样。能在条件改变时修正的准备，比一句反正先拦下来，更能承受时间。
接着，熊彼特会让这张桌子更不安静。他在《资本主义、社会主义与民主》第七、八章，把新的商品、技术与组织带来的变化放在中心。有时真正撼动一家企业的，不是隔壁同样的店便宜一点，而是另一种做事方式，连它赖以存在的地面都换掉了。
他的提醒还不止创新很重要。某些眼前看起来限制竞争的安排，可能在保护长期投入；只截取一个时点，未必看得懂它在变化中的作用。同时，他明确没有把这番分析写成反对一切国家监管，也没有替所有卡特尔担保。不同安排可能产生不同结果。
把这个压力放回苹果城：运维方说，要投入一套新系统，需要较稳定的合同。城里若随时可以无成本撤走，某些投入或许不会发生。市民关心以后换不换得了人，运营商关心今天投下去收不收得回来，两边都不是一句贪心就能打发。
难处正在于，保护投入与保护位置，可能穿着同一件衣服。二十年的合同究竟是在支撑二十年的工程，还是把五年已能回收的投入讲成二十年的封路？这里的数字只是为了看清问题，不是给现实行业定期限。要分辨，得看投入、风险、替代与接续条件，不能只认合同上写着长期。
所以照现在核，不是只看本季利润或本月价格。今天可以取得的证据，也包括长期计划、已经投入的能力、原来承诺与后来变化。还要说清，什么事情发生后，原先的理由需要重看。不断拍下许多张现在的照片，也未必就看懂了一段发展的过程。
我们仍然没有一把尺，能在不确定的时间里准确分开每一次保护与阻挡。承认这一点，会让判断更难，却不会使任何一方免于说明。既不能保证创新迟早会冲开一切，也不能因它尚未发生，就宣判所有等待都只是借口。
还有一个更朴素的反问：是不是只要没有一家把路拿住，人就一定取得生活所需？不一定。粮食很多，许多人仍可能买不起；店家各自正常经营，一种服务仍可能离需要它的人太远。离不开某一家，是取得失败的一种形状，不是全部形状。
假如问题不是集中控制，就不应为了让自己的诊断处处适用，硬找出一个幕后主人。保障怎样安排，谁立了什么规则，怎样执行，供给够不够得着人，仍可以继续问。没有垄断者，不等于没有责任的位置；只是我们已经走到了另一组问题面前。
同样，给大企业多征税，可能把一部分钱分回来，却未必让别人能接替它。反过来，一项具体税制若改变了控制关系，也不能先验地说它只有分钱的作用。先看它实际改变哪件事，再说它承担什么任务，比把某种工具永久归入一只抽屉更可靠。
这把我们带回水务局的续约桌。居民可以希望水便宜、供得稳、系统继续进步，也希望有朝一日说不时，不必先让全城停水。这些希望之间会有代价，也可能互相支持。所谓判断，不是从里面挑一句最大声的，把其余几句都压下去。
与传统对话，也不必把每位作者请来给自己作证。关于数据怎样塑造行为、技术利益怎样分配、信息产业怎样由开放走向封闭，还有许多值得读的书。但转述、书评、书目介绍与通读原著不是一回事。没有读到的部分，应该成为下一次阅读的起点，而不是今天拿来宣布胜负的材料。
法律的回答也要留在它作答的地方。某一市场里有没有达到法定垄断门槛，与一个人的记录能否带走，可能有关，却不等同。法院判了一件事，不能被借来宣布其他问题都已解决；我们认为仍有问题，也不能倒过来改写裁判实际上认定了什么。
这里因此留着几种不同的未完：有的是证据还得查，有的是制度怎么做还要设计，有的是本来就不由这一组文章回答。跨国协作、公司的内部治理、政府自己的权力，都有相邻的工作。说清楚交给哪里，并不等于已经有人替受影响者把事情办好了。
最需要继续做的三问，也可以说得很平常：怎样保护值得做的长期投入，又不让它变成后来者永远进不来的理由；怎样不抹旧账，又不拿旧账替今天所有措施定分量；怎样分回利益，同时检查握着路的位置是否改变。这三问，不靠最后一段好听的话就能结清。
下次通衢再降价，店主仍可以高兴。高兴之后，他也可以问，交易记录能不能好好带走。运维方说需要长期合同，城里可以认真听，也可以问，交接的接口为什么必须永远只有你读得懂。把好处留下，把问题问清，不是对发展冷淡；是不愿把每个人的以后，只交给一个位置的好意。
body_en: Crossways has cut its fees again. A shopkeeper checks the monthly statement and finds a saving he can actually use. Customers are buying more, too. Tell him this is the moment to discuss monopoly, and he may have a reasonable reply: before you explain freedom, could you let my bills come down? An account concerned with people's lives ought to hear that question, not dismiss it as evidence that people misunderstand their interests.

By now, being able to leave, having workable alternatives, and being able to challenge a decision sound familiar. Familiarity creates its own risk. We may start finding the answer wherever we carry the vocabulary. This final essay invites several demanding perspectives into the conversation. The purpose is not to recruit distinguished supporters. It is to discover what our questions illuminate, and what they still cannot settle.

Price is a good place to begin. In Book I, Chapter VII of The Wealth of Nations, Adam Smith contrasts the price obtainable under monopoly with a competitive price constrained by what sellers can ordinarily accept while continuing in business. Restricted supply can make buyers pay more for the seller's protected position. This is a clear route into a real economic burden, not an obsolete concern to be discarded for a more interesting one.

Money saved can change a household's week. It can keep another item on the shopping list or relieve a small business's pressure. A theory should not turn those gains into illusions merely because it wants to introduce an additional measure. The shopkeeper's lower bill belongs in the account. The question is whether it completes the account, rather than whether we can explain it away.

Crossways could lower its fees while still preventing the shopkeeper from taking useful transaction records elsewhere. A competitor might welcome his business but be unable to import the exported files. One condition has improved; another has not. Adding the second question does not require denying the first answer. Nor does this limited comparison warrant describing Smith's entire work as concerned with prices alone.

Imagine a reader asking us to put a value on the migration difficulty. Which records matter? What exactly cannot be imported? How long would rebuilding them take? Might privacy or security justify some restrictions? Those are contemporary questions we must answer, not objections we can pretend Smith addressed to us. A vague appeal to freedom cannot excuse leaving the practical burden unexamined.

Go into the shop and find out. Exporting customer information might expose other people; exporting a list of the shop's own products might present a different issue. An inconvenience is not automatically domination. Yet a monthly saving cannot settle every condition attached to departure. Benefits and dependence need to remain visible together, without either becoming a solvent that dissolves the other.

Louis Brandeis offers another pressure. The title of Chapter VIII of Other People's Money, A Curse of Bigness, can tempt us to hear a simple objection to large firms. A more useful thread in the chapter concerns the means by which size is acquired and the uses to which it is put. Origin and subsequent operation can be examined separately. Neither is reducible to the number of people a business employs.

Suppose a firm once obstructed rivals improperly and later developed a genuinely better service. The improvement need not erase responsibility for the earlier conduct. Equally, an important contribution made years ago cannot authorize every exclusion imposed today. Looking at the present is not agreeing to forget everything before it. A business can deserve credit and still owe an answer, without either judgment being insincere.

Three matters must stay distinct: responsibility for completed conduct, arrangements whose effects continue, and the grounds for measures proposed now. Their connections need working out. This series supplies no universal exchange rate between historical wrongdoing and the strength of a present restriction. Making the distinction is not resolving the case; it prevents us from silently using one finding to decide all three matters.

Brandeis also presses the timing of intervention. The railroad recommendations he discusses give an important place to advance approval and restrictions. Why should a community always wait until a transaction is completed and dependence has matured before asking whether conditions were needed? Preparations made before a relationship hardens can matter as much as remedies designed after harm becomes demonstrable.

Moving earlier, however, does not make a judgment infallible. A premature restriction can obstruct useful cooperation. Those proposing a combination should explain its gains; those proposing constraints should explain their evidence, costs, and alternatives. Preparation that can be revised when conditions change is more demanding, and more valuable, than a standing instruction to block first and ask later.

Joseph Schumpeter makes the conversation less comfortable still. Chapters VII and VIII of Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy emphasize change driven by new products, technologies, and organizations. Competition may arrive by altering the foundations of an established business rather than making an identical product marginally cheaper. Some apparently restrictive arrangements can protect long-term investment. A snapshot may misread their role in that process.

That argument is not an endorsement of every cartel. Schumpeter explicitly distinguishes it from a case against state regulation and rejects indiscriminate conclusions about breaking up businesses. His challenge is serious precisely because outcomes can differ. To invoke innovation is not already to have identified which arrangement sustains it, over what period, at what cost, or to whose benefit.

Return to Apple City's imagined water contract. The operator says that a new system requires a stable agreement. If the city can withdraw at any moment without bearing relevant costs, some investment may never occur. Residents want the ability to replace the operator later; the operator wants a reasonable basis for investing now. Neither interest disappears merely because someone describes its holder as greedy.

Protecting investment and protecting an incumbent's position can wear the same clothes. Does a twenty-year agreement support a project requiring that horizon, or turn an investment recoverable in five years into twenty years of exclusion? These numbers clarify the question; they prescribe no term for a real industry. Costs, risks, alternatives, and handover conditions require examination. The words long term settle none of them.

Assessing present grounds must therefore include the evidence presently available about longer processes: plans, capabilities already built, commitments made, and conditions that have changed. It must also specify what would call the original rationale into question. Repeatedly taking snapshots does not by itself provide a longitudinal understanding. A sequence of confident short-term judgments can still miss what is developing between them.

We do not possess an instrument that infallibly separates investment protection from exclusion while the future remains uncertain. Recognizing that limit makes judgment harder without giving either side immunity. Innovation cannot be assumed eventually to sweep every obstacle away. Nor does its failure to arrive today establish that every request for patience is a pretext. Both claims require more than a convenient story about time.

A different limit appears in a basic question: if no single business controls a route, can everyone obtain what they need? Not necessarily. Plenty of food can coexist with people unable to buy it. Suppliers can behave ordinarily while a service remains beyond the reach of those who need it. Dependence on a concentrated provider is one mechanism of failed access, not an explanation of every such failure.

Where that mechanism is absent, we should not invent a hidden monopolist to rescue a universal diagnosis. Provision, protection, rule-making, and implementation remain open to examination. Who established the conditions? What does the arrangement actually deliver? The absence of a concentrated controller does not establish the absence of responsibility. It marks the point where another line of inquiry must take over.

Taxation raises a related distinction. Returning some of a large firm's earnings to the public might leave its control of a route unchanged. A particular tax could also alter that control, depending on its design. First examine what the measure does. Sharing gains and making a position answerable are not identical tasks, but neither must every instrument be assigned permanently to only one task.

Back at the water authority's renewal meeting, residents can reasonably want affordable water, reliable supply, continued technical improvement, and the ability to refuse one operator without going thirsty. These hopes can support one another or involve genuine costs. Judgment is not choosing the loudest legitimate concern and letting it silence the rest. It is keeping the relationships between them available for examination.

Reading a tradition requires similar care. Questions about data and behavior, the distribution of technological gains, and the closure of information industries deserve further reading. A quotation, a review, and a full book are not interchangeable evidence. Where our reading is incomplete, the next task is to read further, not to manufacture a decisive disagreement or claim that another author has already endorsed our conclusions.

Legal answers also belong to the questions actually decided. Whether power meets a statutory threshold in a specified market can matter greatly without determining every practical condition of leaving a service. A judgment cannot simply be borrowed to close all adjacent questions. Concern about those questions gives us no permission, either, to rewrite what the court found. Respect for an answer includes preserving its scope.

Several kinds of unfinished work remain. Some facts need investigation. Some workable institutions need design. Cross-border coordination, internal corporate governance, and government's own powers call for adjacent inquiries. Assigning a question to the right place is useful, but naming that place is not proof that anyone has already delivered an answer to the people affected.

Three particularly difficult questions survive this conversation. How can worthwhile long-term investment be protected without permanently excluding those who follow? How should responsibility for the past connect to the grounds and strength of action now? And how can sharing the gains be assessed alongside changes to the position that controls access? A graceful conclusion cannot settle these merely by acknowledging them.

When Crossways next cuts its fees, the shopkeeper can still be pleased. He can also ask for records that travel usefully. When the water operator requests a longer contract, the city can listen seriously and still ask why only that operator must forever understand the handover interface. Keeping the benefit and continuing the question is not indifference to progress. It refuses to make everyone's future depend solely on a powerful provider's goodwill.

body_hant: 通衢又降價了。店主算了算，這個月能省下一筆，顧客也多買了些東西。如果有人這時說，先別高興，我們還得談壟斷，他很可能會皺眉：你們談的自由，能不能先讓我少交一點錢？這個反問值得認真聽。否則，一套本來關心人的想法，也可能只關心自己的詞。
讀到這裡，離得開、有的選、問得動，已經成了熟悉的幾句話。可一句話熟悉以後，也會有新的危險：拿到哪裡都覺得自己答對了。最後這一篇，不再添一個萬能答案，而是請幾種有分量的問法進來，讓我們看看手裡的工具，哪裡夠用，哪裡還得往前做。
先從價格說起。斯密在《國富論》第一篇第七章，對照壟斷價格與自由競爭的價格：前者盡量從買者那裡取得高價，後者則受到維持經營所需條件的約束。這是一條清楚的觀察路徑。控制者若能讓東西長期供不應求，顧客便可能為那個位置多付錢。
價格重要，不只是因為它容易畫成圖。多花的錢，會擠掉一家人的別的安排；少花的錢，也真能鬆開一點生活。不能為了突出自己的新問題，就把已經得到的便宜說成幻覺。店主省下的費用、顧客買得起的日用品，都應該留在帳裡。
可是通衢還可以更便宜，同時不讓店主帶走有用的交易記錄。新平台願意接他，舊記錄卻只能導出一堆讀不進新系統的文件。價格那一欄變好了，離開的那一欄沒有。我們需要把第二件事加進去，不必先宣佈第一件事不算數。
這也不是對斯密整部著作下一個只看價格的斷語。我們在這裡借他的一條具體分析，辨清它照到了什麼，再問另一個問題。若一位重視價格的讀者反問，遷移的難處究竟多大、值多少錢、是不是你們想象出來的，那是我們今天必須回答的追問，不是假托古人已經說過的話。
回答應當走到店裡：他需要哪些記錄，新系統到底讀不了什麼，補錄要多久，是否有安全與他人隱私的理由。不能把不方便三個字直接擴成被控制，也不能拿每月便宜二十元，替所有遷移條件作結論。兩筆帳得放到同一張桌上，但不能相互塗掉。
再請進來的，是布蘭代斯。《別人的錢》第八章題為大之詛咒，標題很容易讓人以為，他只要見到大公司就反對。正文中有一條更值得留下的線索：規模如何取得，又被拿來做什麼。形成的手段與使用的方向，是可以分別看的。
這使今天的好用，不能自動洗掉昨天的封路。設若一家企業曾經用不正當的辦法排擠對手，後來確實改進了服務，我們可以承認改進，也可以追究已經發生的事。反過來，它當年的貢獻，也不能給今天的排他安排發一張永久通行證。
看現在，不等於從今天起失憶。過去行為的責任、過去留下而仍在起作用的安排、今天採取什麼措施，至少是三件事。它們有關聯，卻不是同一句話。舊責任怎樣影響今天措施的根據與分量，還需要具體工作；這一組文章沒有替它們算出一條通用換算式。
布蘭代斯的討論也帶來一個時間上的催問：是不是總要等合併完成、依賴長成，再請受影響的人來證明自己受了多少損失？在他援引的鐵路監管建議中，事前批准與限制已經站在很重要的位置。預先留下約束，不只是出事以後的補救。
不過，把時間提早，並不自動使判斷正確。早期限制也可能擋住一次有用的合作。提出合併的一方得說明會帶來什麼，主張約束的一方也得說明擔心什麼、根據何在、代價怎樣。能在條件改變時修正的準備，比一句反正先攔下來，更能承受時間。
接著，熊彼特會讓這張桌子更不安靜。他在《資本主義、社會主義與民主》第七、八章，把新的商品、技術與組織帶來的變化放在中心。有時真正撼動一家企業的，不是隔壁同樣的店便宜一點，而是另一種做事方式，連它賴以存在的地面都換掉了。
他的提醒還不止創新很重要。某些眼前看起來限制競爭的安排，可能在保護長期投入；只截取一個時點，未必看得懂它在變化中的作用。同時，他明確沒有把這番分析寫成反對一切國家監管，也沒有替所有卡特爾擔保。不同安排可能產生不同結果。
把這個壓力放回蘋果城：運維方說，要投入一套新系統，需要較穩定的合同。城裡若隨時可以無成本撤走，某些投入或許不會發生。市民關心以後換不換得了人，運營商關心今天投下去收不收得回來，兩邊都不是一句貪心就能打發。
難處正在於，保護投入與保護位置，可能穿著同一件衣服。二十年的合同究竟是在支撐二十年的工程，還是把五年已能回收的投入講成二十年的封路？這裡的數字只是為了看清問題，不是給現實行業定期限。要分辨，得看投入、風險、替代與接續條件，不能只認合同上寫著長期。
所以照現在核，不是只看本季利潤或本月價格。今天可以取得的證據，也包括長期計劃、已經投入的能力、原來承諾與後來變化。還要說清，什麼事情發生後，原先的理由需要重看。不斷拍下許多張現在的照片，也未必就看懂了一段發展的過程。
我們仍然沒有一把尺，能在不確定的時間裡準確分開每一次保護與阻擋。承認這一點，會讓判斷更難，卻不會使任何一方免於說明。既不能保證創新遲早會衝開一切，也不能因它尚未發生，就宣判所有等待都只是藉口。
還有一個更樸素的反問：是不是只要沒有一家把路拿住，人就一定取得生活所需？不一定。糧食很多，許多人仍可能買不起；店家各自正常經營，一種服務仍可能離需要它的人太遠。離不開某一家，是取得失敗的一種形狀，不是全部形狀。
假如問題不是集中控制，就不應為了讓自己的診斷處處適用，硬找出一個幕後主人。保障怎樣安排，誰立了什麼規則，怎樣執行，供給夠不夠得著人，仍可以繼續問。沒有壟斷者，不等於沒有責任的位置；只是我們已經走到了另一組問題面前。
同樣，給大企業多徵稅，可能把一部分錢分回來，卻未必讓別人能接替它。反過來，一項具體稅制若改變了控制關係，也不能先驗地說它只有分錢的作用。先看它實際改變哪件事，再說它承擔什麼任務，比把某種工具永久歸入一隻抽屜更可靠。
這把我們帶回水務局的續約桌。居民可以希望水便宜、供得穩、系統繼續進步，也希望有朝一日說不時，不必先讓全城停水。這些希望之間會有代價，也可能互相支持。所謂判斷，不是從裡面挑一句最大聲的，把其餘幾句都壓下去。
與傳統對話，也不必把每位作者請來給自己作證。關於資料怎樣塑造行為、技術利益怎樣分配、資訊產業怎樣由開放走向封閉，還有許多值得讀的書。但轉述、書評、書目介紹與通讀原著不是一回事。沒有讀到的部分，應該成為下一次閱讀的起點，而不是今天拿來宣佈勝負的材料。
法律的回答也要留在它作答的地方。某一市場裡有沒有達到法定壟斷門檻，與一個人的記錄能否帶走，可能有關，卻不等同。法院判了一件事，不能被借來宣佈其他問題都已解決；我們認為仍有問題，也不能倒過來改寫裁判實際上認定了什麼。
這裡因此留著幾種不同的未完：有的是證據還得查，有的是制度怎麼做還要設計，有的是本來就不由這一組文章回答。跨國協作、公司的內部治理、政府自己的權力，都有相鄰的工作。說清楚交給哪裡，並不等於已經有人替受影響者把事情辦好了。
最需要繼續做的三問，也可以說得很平常：怎樣保護值得做的長期投入，又不讓它變成後來者永遠進不來的理由；怎樣不抹舊帳，又不拿舊帳替今天所有措施定分量；怎樣分回利益，同時檢查握著路的位置是否改變。這三問，不靠最後一段好聽的話就能結清。
下次通衢再降價，店主仍可以高興。高興之後，他也可以問，交易記錄能不能好好帶走。運維方說需要長期合同，城裡可以認真聽，也可以問，交接的接口為什麼必須永遠只有你讀得懂。把好處留下，把問題問清，不是對發展冷淡；是不願把每個人的以後，只交給一個位置的好意。
